what: Saia is a less-than-truckload carrier: it collects pallets from many shippers, consolidates them at terminals and delivers them, rather than hauling one customer's full trailer.
customers: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers shipping pallets rather than full loads.
money: less-than-truckload shipments across its terminal network
moat: A terminal network is the barrier: it took decades to build and a competitor must have one in every region before it can offer a national service at all.
risks: 31 times earnings while freight demand is weak and its operating ratio has worsened
A large terminal expansion programme is costing money before the volumes arrive
LTL pricing softens when industrial activity slows
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.3B to $3.2B in four years with a 7.9% net margin
Analysts see about 27% upside, with 21 covering the stock
The terminals opened from Yellow's collapse give it national coverage it could not otherwise have bought
watch: The operating ratio and shipments per day as the new terminals fill.
